sanskrit: idaṃ caturdaśaṃ varṣaṃ yan nāpaśyaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram dhanaṃjayaṃ ca govinda yamau taṃ ca vṛkodaram
english: This is the fourteenth year that I have not seen Yudhiṣṭhira, O Govinda, nor Dhanaṃjaya, nor the twins, nor that Vṛkodara.

sanskrit: jīvanāśaṃ pranaṣṭānāṃ śrāddhaṃ kurvanti mānavāḥ arthatas te mama mṛtās teṣāṃ cāhaṃ janārdana
english: Men perform the śrāddha rite for those whose lives are lost and gone — in truth they are as dead to me, and I am as dead to them, O Janārdana.

sanskrit: brūyā mādhava rājānaṃ dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram bhūyāṃs te hīyate dharmo mā putraka vṛthā kṛthāḥ
english: Tell the king, the righteous-souled Yudhiṣṭhira, O Mādhava: 'Your dharma diminishes more and more — do not, my son, act in vain.'

sanskrit: parāśrayā vāsudeva yā jīvāmi dhig astu mām vṛtteḥ kṛpaṇalabdhāyā apratiṣṭhaiva jyāyasī
english: Shame on me, O Vāsudeva, that I live dependent on another's support — a life of homelessness is better than a livelihood wretchedly obtained.

sanskrit: atho dhanaṃjayaṃ brūyā nityodyuktaṃ vṛkodaram yadarthaṃ kṣatriyā sūte tasya kālo 'yam āgataḥ
english: Tell Dhanaṃjaya too, and the ever-striving Vṛkodara: the time for which a kṣatriya woman gives birth has now arrived.

sanskrit: asmiṃś ced āgate kāle kālo vo 'tikramiṣyati lokasaṃbhāvitāḥ santaḥ sunṛśaṃsaṃ kariṣyatha
english: If this moment passes you by, your time will slip away — you who are held in high esteem by the world will commit a most cruel act.

sanskrit: nṛśaṃsena ca vo yuktāṃs tyajeyaṃ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ kāle hi samanuprāpte tyaktavyam api jīvitam
english: If you are tainted by cruelty I would forsake you for all eternity — for when the right moment has arrived, even life itself must be surrendered.

sanskrit: mādrīputrau ca vaktavyau kṣatradharmaratau sadā vikrameṇārjitān bhogān vṛṇītaṃ jīvitād api
english: The two sons of Mādrī, ever devoted to the warrior's duty, must also be told: choose the pleasures won by valor even over life itself.

sanskrit: vikramādhigatā hy arthāḥ kṣatradharmeṇa jīvataḥ mano manuṣyasya sadā prīṇanti puruṣottama
english: For wealth gained through valor, living by the code of the warrior, ever delights the heart of a man, O Puruṣottama.

sanskrit: gatvā brūhi mahābāho sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varam arjunaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ vīraṃ draupadyāḥ padavīṃ cara
english: Go and tell that best of all weapon-bearers, the heroic Pāṇḍava Arjuna, O mighty-armed one: follow the path of Draupadī.

sanskrit: viditau hi tavātyantaṃ kruddhāv iva yathāntakau bhīmārjunau nayetāṃ hi devān api parāṃ gatim
english: For Bhīma and Arjuna, fully known to you, enraged like twin destroyers, could bring even the gods to their final end.

sanskrit: tayoś caitad avajñānaṃ yat sā kṛṣṇā sabhāṃ gatā duḥśāsanaś ca karṇaś ca paruṣāṇy abhyabhāṣatām
english: This was the insult to both of them — that Kṛṣṇā was dragged into the assembly and Duḥśāsana and Karṇa spoke harsh words to her.

sanskrit: duryodhano bhīmasenam abhyagacchan manasvinam paśyatāṃ kurumukhyānāṃ tasya drakṣyati yat phalam
english: Duryodhana went against the high-minded Bhīmasena before the eyes of the Kuru chiefs — he shall see the fruit of that act.

sanskrit: na hi vairaṃ samāsādya praśāmyati vṛkodaraḥ sucirād api bhīmasya na hi vairaṃ praśāmyati yāvadantaṃ na nayati śātravāñ śatrukarśanaḥ
english: For Vṛkodara does not calm down once enmity has been taken up — Bhīma's enmity does not cool even after long ages, not until he brings his enemies to their final end, that crusher of foes.

sanskrit: na duḥkhaṃ rājyaharaṇaṃ na ca dyūte parājayaḥ pravrājanaṃ ca putrāṇāṃ na me tad duḥkhakāraṇam
english: The taking of the kingdom is not my grief, nor the defeat at dice, nor the exile of my sons — those are not the cause of my sorrow.

sanskrit: yat tu sā bṛhatī śyāmā ekavastrā sabhāṃ gatā aśṛṇot paruṣā vācas tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim
english: But that she — tall, dark, clad in a single garment — was dragged into the assembly and heard those harsh words: what could be more painful than that?

sanskrit: strīdharmiṇī varārohā kṣatradharmaratā sadā nādhyagacchat tathā nāthaṃ kṛṣṇā nāthavatī satī
english: Though a virtuous woman of the finest form, ever devoted to the warrior's code, Kṛṣṇā found no protector then, though she had protectors and was a chaste wife.

sanskrit: yasyā mama saputrāyās tvaṃ nātho madhusūdana rāmaś ca balināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ pradyumnaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: You are the protector of her and my sons, O Madhusūdana, and Rāma the foremost of the strong, and Pradyumna the great warrior.

sanskrit: sāham evaṃvidhaṃ duḥkhaṃ sahe 'dya puruṣottama bhīme jīvati durdharṣe vijaye cāpalāyini
english: I endure such grief even now, O Puruṣottama, while Bhīma the unconquerable lives, and Vijaya the swift.

sanskrit: tata āśvāsayām āsa putrādhibhir abhiplutām pitṛṣvasāraṃ śocantīṃ śauriḥ pārthasakhaḥ pṛthām
english: Then Śauri, the friend of the Pārthas, comforted Pṛthā his father's sister, who was overwhelmed with grief for her sons and weeping.

sanskrit: kā nu sīmantinī tvādṛg lokeṣv asti pitṛṣvasaḥ śūrasya rājño duhitā ājamīḍhakulaṃ gatā
english: What woman in all the worlds is like you, O father's sister? Daughter of the king Śūra, who has entered the lineage of Ājamīḍha.

sanskrit: mahākulīnā bhavatī hradād dhradam ivāgatā īśvarī sarvakalyāṇī bhartrā paramapūjitā
english: You are of the highest lineage, having passed from one illustrious family to another like a lake flowing into a lake, a sovereign lady, blessed with every auspiciousness, supremely honored by your husband.

sanskrit: vīrasūr vīrapatnī ca sarvaiḥ samuditā guṇaiḥ sukhaduḥkhe mahāprājñe tvādṛśī soḍhum arhati
english: Mother of heroes, wife of a hero, endowed with every virtue — one such as you, O greatly wise one, is fit to endure both joy and sorrow.

sanskrit: nidrātandrī krodhaharṣau kṣutpipāse himātapau etāni pārthā nirjitya nityaṃ vīrāḥ sukhe ratāḥ
english: The Pārthas have conquered sleep and sloth, anger and exultation, hunger and thirst, cold and heat — ever heroic, they delight in well-being.

sanskrit: tyaktagrāmyasukhāḥ pārthā nityaṃ vīrasukhapriyāḥ na te svalpena tuṣyeyur mahotsāhā mahābalāḥ
english: The Pārthas have abandoned common pleasures and always love the joy of heroes — those of great enterprise and great strength would not be satisfied with little.

sanskrit: antaṃ dhīrā niṣevante madhyaṃ grāmyasukhapriyāḥ uttamāṃś ca parikleśān bhogāṃś cātīva mānuṣān
english: The resolute pursue extremes; lovers of common pleasure pursue the middle — the greatest hardships and pleasures far surpassing the human.

sanskrit: anteṣu remire dhīrā na te madhyeṣu remire antaprāptiṃ sukhām āhur duḥkham antaram antayoḥ
english: The steadfast delight in the extremes, not in the middle — they say that reaching the extreme is bliss, and that the space between extremes is suffering.

sanskrit: abhivādayanti bhavatīṃ pāṇḍavāḥ saha kṛṣṇayā ātmānaṃ ca kuśalinaṃ nivedyāhur anāmayam
english: The Pāṇḍavas salute you together with Kṛṣṇā, and report themselves well and free from illness.

sanskrit: arogān sarvasiddhārthān kṣipraṃ drakṣyasi pāṇḍavān īśvarān sarvalokasya hatāmitrāñ śriyā vṛtān
english: You will soon see the Pāṇḍavas in full health, with all their purposes achieved, lords of all the world, their enemies slain, and surrounded by prosperity.

sanskrit: evam āśvāsitā kuntī pratyuvāca janārdanam putrādhibhir abhidhvastā nigṛhyābuddhijaṃ tamaḥ
english: Thus comforted, Kuntī, overwhelmed by grief for her sons but restraining the darkness born of the unwise mind, replied to Janārdana.

sanskrit: yad yat teṣāṃ mahābāho pathyaṃ syān madhusūdana yathā yathā tvaṃ manyethāḥ kuryāḥ kṛṣṇa tathā tathā
english: Whatever may be beneficial for them, O mighty-armed Madhusūdana, whatever you think proper, O Kṛṣṇa — do precisely that.

sanskrit: avilopena dharmasya anikṛtyā paraṃtapa prabhāvajñāsmi te kṛṣṇa satyasyābhijanasya ca
english: Without transgressing dharma, without deceit, O scorcher of foes — I know your power, O Kṛṣṇa, and your truth and your lineage.

sanskrit: vyavasthāyāṃ ca mitreṣu buddhivikramayos tathā tvam eva naḥ kule dharmas tvaṃ satyaṃ tvaṃ tapo mahat
english: In steadfastness toward friends, in wisdom and valor alike — you alone are the dharma of our family, you are the truth, you are the great austerity.

sanskrit: tvaṃ trātā tvaṃ mahad brahma tvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam yathaivāttha tathaivaitat tvayi satyaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: You are the protector, you are the great brahman, in you everything is established — as you have said, so it will indeed prove true in you.

sanskrit: tām āmantrya ca govindaḥ kṛtvā cābhipradakṣiṇam prātiṣṭhata mahābāhur duryodhanagṛhān prati
english: Having taken leave of her, and having circumambulated her, Govinda the mighty-armed set out toward the house of Duryodhana.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pṛthām āmantrya govindaḥ kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam duryodhanagṛhaṃ śaurir abhyagacchad ariṃdamaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having taken leave of Pṛthā and circumambulated her, Govinda, Śauri the subduer of enemies, proceeded to the house of Duryodhana.

sanskrit: lakṣmyā paramayā yuktaṃ puraṃdaragṛhopamam tasya kakṣyā vyatikramya tisro dvāḥsthair avāritaḥ
english: Endowed with supreme splendor, comparable to the dwelling of Purandara — he passed through its three inner courts unhindered by the gate-keepers.

sanskrit: tato 'bhraghanasaṃkāśaṃ girikūṭam ivocchritam śriyā jvalantaṃ prāsādam āruroha mahāyaśāḥ
english: Then the greatly glorious one ascended the palace that resembled a dense mass of clouds, that rose like a mountain peak, blazing with splendor.

sanskrit: tatra rājasahasraiś ca kurubhiś cābhisaṃvṛtam dhārtarāṣṭraṃ mahābāhuṃ dadarśāsīnam āsane
english: There he saw Dhārtarāṣṭra, the mighty-armed, seated on his throne, surrounded by thousands of kings and the Kurus.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanaṃ ca karṇaṃ ca śakuniṃ cāpi saubalam duryodhanasamīpe tān āsanasthān dadarśa saḥ
english: He saw Duḥśāsana, Karṇa, and Śakuni the son of Subala, all seated near Duryodhana.

sanskrit: abhyāgacchati dāśārhe dhārtarāṣṭro mahāyaśāḥ udatiṣṭhat sahāmātyaḥ pūjayan madhusūdanam
english: As the Dāśārha approached, the greatly glorious Dhārtarāṣṭra rose with his ministers, honoring Madhusūdana.

sanskrit: sametya dhārtarāṣṭreṇa sahāmātyena keśavaḥ rājabhis tatra vārṣṇeyaḥ samāgacchad yathāvayaḥ
english: Meeting with Dhārtarāṣṭra and his ministers, Keśava the Vārṣṇeya came together with the kings in their proper order of precedence.

sanskrit: tatra jāmbūnadamayaṃ paryaṅkaṃ supariṣkṛtam vividhāstaraṇāstīrṇam abhyupāviśad acyutaḥ
english: There Acyuta seated himself on a couch made of gold, excellently adorned and spread with various coverings.

sanskrit: tasmin gāṃ madhuparkaṃ ca upahṛtya janārdane nivedayām āsa tadā gṛhān rājyaṃ ca kauravaḥ
english: Offering him a cow and madhuparka, the Kaurava then presented to Janārdana his house and his kingdom.

sanskrit: tatra govindam āsīnaṃ prasannādityavarcasam upāsāṃ cakrire sarve kuravo rājabhiḥ saha
english: There all the Kurus together with the kings attended upon Govinda seated there, resplendent as the clear sun.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā vārṣṇeyaṃ jayatāṃ varam nyamantrayad bhojanena nābhyanandac ca keśavaḥ
english: Then king Duryodhana invited the Vārṣṇeya, the foremost of the victorious, to dine — but Keśava did not accept with delight.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ kṛṣṇam abravīd rājasaṃsadi mṛdupūrvaṃ śaṭhodarkaṃ karṇam ābhāṣya kauravaḥ
english: Then Duryodhana spoke to Kṛṣṇa in the royal assembly, the Kaurava addressing Karṇa first with soft and then with crafty words.

sanskrit: kasmād annāni pānāni vāsāṃsi śayanāni ca tvadartham upanītāni nāgrahīs tvaṃ janārdana
english: Why have you not accepted, O Janārdana, the food and drink, the robes and beds that have been brought for your sake?

sanskrit: ubhayoś cādadaḥ sāhyam ubhayoś ca hite rataḥ saṃbandhī dayitaś cāsi dhṛtarāṣṭrasya mādhava
english: You give your help to both sides, you are devoted to the good of both — you are also a relative and a beloved one of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi govinda dharmārthau vettha tattvena sarvaśaḥ tatra kāraṇam icchāmi śrotuṃ cakragadādhara
english: For you, O Govinda, know dharma and artha truly in every respect — I wish to hear the reason, O bearer of discus and mace.

sanskrit: sa evam ukto govindaḥ pratyuvāca mahāmanāḥ oghameghasvanaḥ kāle pragṛhya vipulaṃ bhujam
english: Thus addressed, Govinda the great-souled replied, his voice like the roar of surging clouds, raising his broad arm at the right moment.

sanskrit: anambūkṛtam agrastam anirastam asaṃkulam rājīvanetro rājānaṃ hetumadvākyam uttamam
english: The lotus-eyed one spoke to the king a supremely reasoned speech — unhurried, uninterrupted, unrejected, unconfused.

sanskrit: kṛtārthā bhuñjate dūtāḥ pūjāṃ gṛhṇanti caiva hi kṛtārthaṃ māṃ sahāmātyas tvam arciṣyasi bhārata
english: Envoys eat and receive honor when their mission is accomplished — when my mission is accomplished, you with your ministers shall honor me then, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca dhārtarāṣṭro janārdanam na yuktaṃ bhavatāsmāsu pratipattum asāṃpratam
english: Thus spoken to, Dhārtarāṣṭra replied to Janārdana: It is not right for you to behave toward us in this unseemly manner.

sanskrit: kṛtārthaṃ cākṛtārthaṃ ca tvāṃ vayaṃ madhusūdana yatāmahe pūjayituṃ govinda na ca śaknumaḥ
english: Whether your purpose is accomplished or not, we endeavor to honor you, O Madhusūdana, O Govinda — and we cannot refrain from it.

sanskrit: na ca tat kāraṇaṃ vidmo yasmin no madhusūdana pūjāṃ kṛtāṃ prīyamāṇair nāmaṃsthāḥ puruṣottama
english: Nor do we know the reason, O Madhusūdana, why you, O Puruṣottama, do not accept the honor done to you by us with joy.

sanskrit: vairaṃ no nāsti bhavatā govinda na ca vigrahaḥ sa bhavān prasamīkṣyaitan nedṛśaṃ vaktum arhati
english: We have no enmity with you, O Govinda, nor any quarrel — you yourself, upon reflection, ought not to say such a thing.

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca dhārtarāṣṭraṃ janārdanaḥ abhivīkṣya sahāmātyaṃ dāśārhaḥ prahasann iva
english: Thus addressed, Janārdana replied to Dhārtarāṣṭra, the Dāśārha glancing at him and his ministers with something like a smile.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ kāmān na saṃrambhān na dveṣān nārthakāraṇāt na hetuvādāl lobhād vā dharmaṃ jahyāṃ kathaṃ cana
english: I would never abandon dharma out of desire, out of passion, out of hatred, for the sake of gain, on account of argument, or out of greed — never in any way.

sanskrit: saṃprītibhojyāny annāni āpadbhojyāni vā punaḥ na ca saṃprīyase rājan na cāpy āpadgatā vayam
english: Food is eaten in joy or in distress — but you are not joyful toward us, O king, nor are we in distress.

sanskrit: akasmād dviṣase rājañ janmaprabhṛti pāṇḍavān priyānuvartino bhrātṝn sarvaiḥ samuditān guṇaiḥ
english: Without cause, O king, you have hated the Pāṇḍavas from birth — brothers who follow after you with affection, endowed with every virtue.

sanskrit: akasmāc caiva pārthānāṃ dveṣaṇaṃ nopapadyate dharme sthitāḥ pāṇḍaveyāḥ kas tān kiṃ vaktum arhati
english: And such causeless hatred of the Pārthas is not fitting — the Pāṇḍavas are established in dharma; who could rightfully say anything against them?

sanskrit: yas tān dveṣṭi sa māṃ dveṣṭi yas tān anu sa mām anu aikātmyaṃ māṃ gataṃ viddhi pāṇḍavair dharmacāribhiḥ
english: Whoever hates them hates me; whoever follows them follows me — know that I am one in soul with the Pāṇḍavas who walk in dharma.

sanskrit: kāmakrodhānuvartī hi yo mohād virurutsate guṇavantaṃ ca yo dveṣṭi tam āhuḥ puruṣādhamam
english: One who, following desire and anger, out of delusion seeks to injure, and who hates the virtuous — they call him the vilest of men.

sanskrit: yaḥ kalyāṇaguṇāñ jñātīn mohāl lobhād didṛkṣate so 'jitātmājitakrodho na ciraṃ tiṣṭhati śriyam
english: One who, out of delusion and greed, looks upon his kinsmen who possess noble qualities with ill will — he who has not conquered himself and not conquered his anger does not long hold on to prosperity.

sanskrit: atha yo guṇasaṃpannān hṛdayasyāpriyān api priyeṇa kurute vaśyāṃś ciraṃ yaśasi tiṣṭhati
english: But one who treats those endowed with virtue, even those not dear to his heart, with affection and makes them his own — he long abides in glory.

sanskrit: sarvam etad abhoktavyam annaṃ duṣṭābhisaṃhitam kṣattur ekasya bhoktavyam iti me dhīyate matiḥ
english: All this food, offered with wicked intent, is not to be eaten — only at Kṣattā's alone should one eat, so my mind is resolved.

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahābāhur duryodhanam amarṣaṇam niścakrāma tataḥ śubhrād dhārtarāṣṭraniveśanāt
english: Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed one departed from the splendid dwelling of Dhārtarāṣṭra, leaving the impassioned Duryodhana behind.

sanskrit: niryāya ca mahābāhur vāsudevo mahāmanāḥ niveśāya yayau veśma vidurasya mahātmanaḥ
english: And having departed, Vāsudeva the mighty-armed, the great-souled one, proceeded to lodge at the house of the great-souled Vidura.

sanskrit: tam abhyagacchad droṇaś ca kṛpo bhīṣmo 'tha bāhlikaḥ kuravaś ca mahābāhuṃ vidurasya gṛhe sthitam
english: Droṇa, Kṛpa, Bhīṣma, Bāhlika, and the Kurus came to him, the mighty-armed one, as he stood in Vidura's house.

sanskrit: te 'bhigamyābruvaṃs tatra kuravo madhusūdanam nivedayāmo vārṣṇeya saratnāṃs te gṛhānvayam
english: The Kurus, having approached, said to Madhusūdana there: We present to you, O Vārṣṇeya, our houses along with their jewels.

sanskrit: tān uvāca mahātejāḥ kauravān madhusūdanaḥ sarve bhavanto gacchantu sarvā me 'pacitiḥ kṛtā
english: Madhusūdana, of great splendor, said to the Kauravas: You may all depart — all honor has been done to me.

sanskrit: yāteṣu kuruṣu kṣattā dāśārham aparājitam abhyarcayām āsa tadā sarvakāmaiḥ prayatnavān
english: When the Kurus had departed, Kṣattā then diligently honored the invincible Dāśārha with all desired objects.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṣattānnapānāni śucīni guṇavanti ca upāharad anekāni keśavāya mahātmane
english: Then Kṣattā offered many pure and excellent foods and drinks to the great-souled Keśava.

sanskrit: tair tarpayitvā prathamaṃ brāhmaṇān madhusūdanaḥ vedavidbhyo dadau kṛṣṇaḥ paramadraviṇāny api
english: Having first satisfied the brahmins with those, Kṛṣṇa Madhusūdana also gave the finest of riches to those who knew the Vedas.

sanskrit: tato 'nuyāyibhiḥ sārdhaṃ marudbhir iva vāsavaḥ vidurānnāni bubhuje śucīni guṇavanti ca
english: Then, together with his followers like Vāsava with the Maruts, he partook of Vidura's food — pure and excellent.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca taṃ bhuktavantam āśvastaṃ niśāyāṃ viduro 'bravīt nedaṃ samyag vyavasitaṃ keśavāgamanaṃ tava
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When he had eaten and was at ease, Vidura said to him in the night: This coming of Keśava is not a well-considered undertaking of yours.

sanskrit: arthadharmātigo mūḍhaḥ saṃrambhī ca janārdana mānaghno mānakāmaś ca vṛddhānāṃ śāsanātigaḥ
english: He transgresses artha and dharma, he is deluded and passionate, O Janārdana — he is a destroyer of honor and craver of honor, and he transgresses the counsel of elders.

sanskrit: dharmaśāstrātigo mando durātmā pragrahaṃ gataḥ aneyaḥ śreyasāṃ pāpo dhārtarāṣṭro janārdana
english: He transgresses the dharmaśāstras, he is dull and evil-souled, obstinate and unyielding — Dhārtarāṣṭra is wicked and incapable of being led toward what is good, O Janārdana.

sanskrit: kāmātmā prājñamānī ca mitradhruk sarvaśaṅkitaḥ akartā cākṛtajñaś ca tyaktadharmaḥ priyānṛtaḥ
english: He is enslaved to desire, fancies himself wise, a betrayer of friends, suspicious of everyone, a man of no action, ungrateful, one who has abandoned dharma and is fond of falsehood.
